items.articleText: formafantasma on research, design, and the exhibition space For Formafantasma , the Milan- and Rotterdam-based studio founded by Andrea Trimarchi and Simone Farresin, exhibition design starts with looking closely at the relationship between the artworks, the building, the institution, and the people moving through it. The duo’s research-driven practice often looks at materials, culture, and the relationship between tradition and contemporary production, and they bring the same curiosity to exhibition-making. They look for what they call ‘the tension’ in a project — the moments when the artworks, architecture, curatorial idea, and established ways of displaying art don’t quite line up. ‘There is no fixed methodology, because exhibition design is always relational,’ Formafantasma tells designboom . Research and design happen at the same time in the duo’s process. The studio looks at the artworks, their material and historical context, the building they will be shown in, and the conventions of display, while also testing walls, materials, sightlines, and other ways of organizing the space. Sometimes, a seemingly pragmatic decision can reveal the larger question. ‘An apparently pragmatic decision, a wall, a fabric, a particular sightline, reveals a conceptual question that becomes central to the project,’ they explain. The Shakers: A World in the Making at Vitra Design Museum, Weil am Rhein | image by Bernhard Strauss, courtesy of Vitra Design Museum challenging the supposedly neutral exhibition space That way of working also leads Formafantasma to question one of the most familiar conventions of contemporary exhibition-making: neutrality. The white cube can appear to disappear around an artwork, but the studio argues that its familiarity does not make it neutral. ‘A white plaster wall is no less designed than a metal or textile wall,’ they tell us. ‘It has simply become so familiar within contemporary art that we have stopped seeing it as a choice.’ Their exhibitions of Caravaggio and Bernini at the Rijksmuseum in Amsterdam and Mike Kelley at Moderna Museet show how they approach this idea differently depending on the work. For Caravaggio and Bernini, they moved away from the darkness and theatrical lighting associated with the artists, using an exhibition language closer to the white cube. With Mike Kelley, they did almost the opposite, bringing the industrial character of the museum into the foreground through metal panels. In both cases, the architecture around the works is treated as part of the exhibition and not as something that fades into the background. ‘The response therefore cannot precede the question,’ Andrea Trimarchi and Simone Farresin explain . ‘It emerges from looking very closely at what is already there.’ For the studio, the objective is to identify the particular spatial conditions that might make relationships within each project more visible or more complicated. ‘We are less interested in finding a visual language that will unify everything than in understanding what spatial condition might make the relationships within an exhibition more legible or more complex,’ the duo shares with designboom. This also explains their interest in the history of display itself. The way objects are exhibited is never simply a technical matter. ‘We have become increasingly interested in the exhibition itself as an object of inquiry: why a wall looks the way it does, why information occupies a particular position, why visitors are expected to move or sit in particular ways, why some materials appear neutral while others become immediately visible,’ they add. The Shakers: A World in the Making at Vitra Design Museum, Weil am Rhein | image by Bernhard Strauss, courtesy of Vitra Design Museum turning curatorial ideas into spatial conditions This relationship between concept and physical space is evident in Formafantasma’s work for the 2026 Diriyah Contemporary Art Biennale. Curators Nora Razian and Sabih Ahmed were thinking about movement, migration, oral transmission, and different forms of passage. The Biennale’s setting in the JAX district, meanwhile, consisted of very large industrial spaces. Formafantasma introduced porous textile partitions and wooden structures that established boundaries without severing one space from another. Visitors could often perceive another work, room, or presence through the architecture. ‘The curatorial idea of movement therefore wasn’t represented symbolically; it began to affect how boundaries themselves behaved,’ the studio highlights. Instead of translating a curatorial idea into an obvious visual metaphor, Formafantasma allows it to influence the physical organization of the exhibition. The conceptual and the practical develop alongside one another, a process that applies to questions that might initially appear purely technical, such as whether a work can tolerate daylight, how much acoustic separation a sound work requires, what should be visible behind an artwork, where visitors can rest, and how much material should be introduced for an exhibition that will exist for only a few months. ‘Conceptual questions and technical questions are not separate for us,’ they say. ‘The exhibition emerges through their negotiation.’ The Shakers: A World in the Making at Vitra Design Museum, Weil am Rhein | image by Martin Schgaguler, courtesy of Vitra Design Museum providing structure without prescribing interpretation Visitor movement is another area where Formafantasma resists the idea of complete control. items.articleText: An article from Sponsored Enjoy e-commerce delivery at the speed of flight Published Sept. 21, 2026 Share Copy link Email LinkedIn X/Twitter Facebook Print Fizkes/Shutterstock.com Sponsored content By SmartKargo SPONSORED CONTENT BY Peak season logistics: A SmartKargo perspective on preparing for the surge Every peak season tests the same thing: whether a brand’s logistics network can absorb a sudden spike in demand without breaking its promises to customers. Order volumes climb fast, delivery windows shrink and carrier capacity tightens everywhere at once — often right when every other shipper is fighting for the same space. At SmartKargo, we work with e-commerce brands and logistics partners navigating exactly this kind of pressure, both domestically and across borders, and the ones who come through strongest are rarely scrambling in November. They’ve treated peak readiness as a plan, not a panic response. Start with the forecast Good planning starts months out, with historical sales data, marketing calendars and demand signals mapped against inventory and fulfillment capacity. Brands that know which SKUs will move fastest can position inventory closer to demand and lock in transport capacity before rates spike. That includes capacity across every leg of the journey, not just the final mile, since carriers and customs processes tighten at the same time. Waiting until volumes are already climbing usually means paying more for less reliable space. Stress-test fulfillment before wolume hits Warehouse operations need the same discipline. Picking lanes, packing stations and dispatch queues that run fine in a normal month can seize up under peak load. Running orders through the system at simulated peak volume, dedicating stations to fast-moving promotional SKUs and cross-training staff for exception handling all reduce the errors that pressure tends to expose. The goal isn’t perfection under stress, it’s knowing where the system breaks first, before the surge finds it for you. Where Deliver Direct fits in Capacity is where a lot of peak season strategies fall apart, because carrier networks congest at the exact moment brands need them most. That’s the gap Deliver Direct is built to close. By combining scheduled air movement with local pickup and dock-to-door delivery — backed by real-time tracking, proactive notifications and proof of delivery — Deliver Direct gives shippers a way to move volume through the network without leaning entirely on ground carriers that are already stretched thin. Splitting volume across modes like this doesn’t just add capacity; it removes the single point of failure that turns one carrier’s bad week into a brand’s bad quarter. That kind of redundancy is often what keeps delivery promises intact when a single mode would have buckled. deliver-e: Built for the cross-border surge Cross-border adds another layer to peak season pressure that’s easy to underestimate. According to deliver-e’s own research , cross-border e-commerce is growing faster than global e-commerce overall , which means a growing share of peak season order volume isn’t just crossing town, it’s crossing borders. That shifts the operational math. Customs clearance, international carrier handoffs and cross-border tracking all need to hold up under the same order spikes as everything else, and a delay at a border crossing during peak week is harder to route around than a delay on a domestic leg. deliver-e is SmartKargo’s answer to that specific pressure, giving e-commerce brands a way to keep cross-border orders moving and visible during the exact weeks when international demand climbs alongside domestic demand. For brands that treat cross-border as a smaller, secondary channel the rest of the year, peak season is usually when that assumption gets tested hardest. Domestic speed, cross-border reach Put together, Deliver Direct and deliver-e cover the two directions peak season volume actually moves in: fast, trackable delivery within a region, and cross-border orders that need to clear customs and change carriers without losing visibility along the way. A brand running one peak season promotion across multiple markets is really running two logistics problems at once, and treating them as one plan is what keeps a delay in one lane from becoming a customer service problem in the other. Turning pressure into advantage None of this replaces a solid post-peak review. Once the rush passes, the brands that come out ahead measure on-time delivery, order accuracy and return rates against the plan they made, breaking domestic and cross-border performance out separately, then feed those lessons into next year’s forecast. Peak season will keep testing logistics networks every year. With disciplined forecasting, fulfillment readiness and a network like SmartKargo’s built for both domestic and cross-border volume, that test gets a lot more predictable. AI OpenAI forms math advisory group as its AI resolves more than 100 open problems Aditya Mehta 1:15 PM PDT · September 21, 2026 On Monday, OpenAI announced a new independent advisory group hosted at the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton, New Jersey. Called the Advisory Group on Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence , the group is meant to give mathematicians more input into the company’s math-oriented research. “This group will serve as a bridge to the mathematical community and broader public, giving mathematicians a voice in how we move forward,” the post reads. The announcement comes after the abrupt publication of a solution to the Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize problem . As part of the announcement of the new group, OpenAI also claims that the same internal model has resolved more than 100 additional open problems across most areas of mathematics. Many prominent mathematicians have taken issue with the frenzied pace of those results. Earlier this month, 25 Fields Medal-winning mathematicians signed an open letter arguing that AI labs are threatening their intellectual work as they seek to one-up each other with solutions to famous math problems. True to its name, OpenAI’s new group will mostly serve in an advisory capacity, assessing the significance of new results and coordinating their release. While members won’t be paid, they can offer unsolicited advice, go public with their views, and control their own membership, giving them a measure of independence from the company. However, the group won’t be given leeway to slow down or redirect OpenAI’s ongoing mathematical research. As the blog post puts it, “the group will not be responsible for advising us on how to pace our internal progress on mathematics.” The Institute for Advanced Study emphasized this point in its own announcement. “Although we will give advice, we do not have decision making power at any AI company, and the responsibility for the decisions made by any company will rest with that company,” said the institute in a press release. Nine prominent mathematicians have been named as initial members of the group. Notably, only one of the members — IAS’s Camillo De Lellis — also signed the Fields Medalists’ letter. items.articleText: This is today’s edition of The Download , our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. The US spent billions on border surveillance. Why can’t it catch people before they die? When José Morales Bernal crossed the border into the US in April 2024, the day before his 32nd birthday, he was within range of three surveillance towers equipped with cameras and AI to automatically detect and track people. If the system worked as intended, Morales should have been apprehended. If he needed medical help, agents were trained to provide it. None of that happened. Instead, Morales died just 360 feet from the closest tower. It was local landfill workers, rather than Border Patrol, who first spotted him. An autopsy concluded that he had died of “environmental exposure.” A first-of-its-kind investigation by MIT Technology Review reveals that deaths like Morales’s are startlingly common. After mapping nearly 4,000 locations where human remains were found against information on nearly 600 surveillance towers, we discovered that a humanitarian crisis at the border has unfolded in view of the government’s own cameras. Read our full investigation into the deadly failings of the virtual wall . —James O’Donnell and Eileen Guo Learn more: As part of our 15-month investigation, we created the first comprehensive map of deaths near US-Mexico border surveillance towers. Take a look at that map , and read about how we made it . The US government is about to spend another $1 billion to triple the virtual wall’s size, yet we found it has systemic flaws: broken towers, algorithms that failed to detect people and agents who simply did not respond to alerts. Here are four ideas for what Customs and Border Protection should do to rectify those failures. An analysis by the Times of San Diego found at least 138 cases since 2022 in which migrants’ remains were found within the nominal range of a nearby surveillance tower. A separate MIT Technology Review analysis estimated that more than half of those people were likely within a tower’s field of view. Gómez Hernández was one of them. Here’s her story, written by our partners at Times of San Diego . All of these stories are part of Dying on Camera , our new series investigating the failures of border surveillance technology and their human cost. One more thing AI is pushing the limits of the physical world Architecture often assumes a binary between built projects and theoretical ones. What physics allows in actual buildings is vastly different from what architects can imagine and design. But the latest advancements in AI have prompted a surge in the theoretical. That shift was on display at an exhibition at Brooklyn’s Pratt Institute, which brought together works from more than 30 practitioners exploring AI’s experimental, generative and collaborative potential to open up new areas of architectural inquiry. items.articleText: Innovation Nvidia’s free AI model could push the UAE closer to the U.S. The Emirates owns the machines but rents the intelligence. Nvidia’s next free AI model could change that. Rest of World/iStock Rest of World/iStock By Indranil Ghosh 21 September 2026 Nvidia’s chips are driving the United Arab Emirates’ rise as an artificial-intelligence power. Next on offer is free software, a model built to rival China’s best. Last month, Nvidia spent $7 billion to buy a stake in U.S. coding startup Poolside and license the tools it uses to build AI models. The new model is due by the end of the year for anyone to download for free, and it is aimed at buyers already running Nvidia hardware, Marc Einstein, an analyst at Counterpoint Research, told Rest of World . Few countries fit that description better than the UAE, whose flagship data center will run on 400,000 Nvidia chips . For years the UAE positioned itself as neutral ground between the U.S. and China, buying chips from the former and, until recently, equipment from the latter. It built its own free model, Falcon, to avoid relying on imported software. That neutrality has been fading since G42, the state-backed AI company, cut its Chinese ties to win Nvidia’s chips. It would narrow further if the country also opts for the new model. “The last missing piece was the model layer,” Mohammed Soliman, a senior fellow at the Middle East Institute, a foreign-policy think tank in Washington, told Rest of World . “Nvidia already owns the chips. Now it is scaling the factory that produces the models that run on those chips, and it is releasing them as open weights.” Build or rent? The two institutions leading the UAE’s AI push each have their own view on whether to build sovereign AI models from scratch or lean on existing technology from other companies. The Technology Innovation Institute, the government lab behind Falcon, insists on building its own models from the ground up, while G42, which runs the UAE’s AI infrastructure, has aligned itself with Nvidia’s push for free models. The value is not limited to the models we ultimately produce, but it lies in mastering the underlying technology and retaining control.” Hakim Hacid, chief researcher, Technology Innovation Institute “As a model-building lab, we believe that maintaining diversity in AI perspectives, and preserving full technological sovereignty, requires a strong, homegrown foundation,” Hakim Hacid, TII’s chief researcher, told Rest of World . “The value is not limited to the models we ultimately produce, but it lies in mastering the underlying technology and retaining control across the entire AI stack.” G42 did not answer Rest of World ’s questions about whether it would use Nvidia’s model. The company has been an early supporter of Nvidia’s push to give away powerful models. In July, Nvidia formed an alliance around the argument that countries need AI models they can inspect and control, and G42 joined immediately, becoming the only Gulf company to do so. “Frontier open models are an essential part of that future, alongside frontier closed models, with security, trust and sovereign control designed in from the start rather than bolted on later,” G42’s CEO, Peng Xiao, wrote on X at the time. Building on someone else’s model need not mean giving up control, Soliman said. Sovereignty in AI is a matter of degree rather than an all-or-nothing choice, he said. “Sovereignty was never about inventing the foundational model from scratch,” Soliman said. “It is about the model’s weights, how you fine-tune the data, and, most importantly at this stage, your ability to serve these models to users in the UAE and other markets.” The U.S. government approved sales of Nvidia’s most advanced chips to the UAE after G42 sold its stakes in Chinese technology companies two years ago. In July, it placed the UAE in the group of countries it treats as its closest technology allies. The software running on those chips is mostly rented from U.S. companies, which decide what the models may do and who may use them. Falcon was meant to be the exception. TII built it in 2023 as a free alternative to models from the U.S. and China, and it ranked first this year on Counterpoint’s index of state-backed models. Saudi Arabia, which is competing with the UAE to become the region’s AI hub, has taken a different route. Humain, the state AI company, is cleared to buy tens of thousands of Nvidia chips, and introduced an Arabic model this month that it had commissioned from a Chinese lab. A year earlier, it had launched one it said was built from scratch in the kingdom. “It shows there’s little full-stack lock-in: The Saudis are using Chinese AI models to build their own models, while using U.S. chips to develop and run them,” Sam Winter-Levy, a senior fellow at the think tank Carnegie Endowment for International Peace, told Rest of World . “These states have strong incentives to hedge and will continue to do so for as long as they can.” Nvidia’s Nemotron Nvidia has its own reasons for wanting countries to take the upcoming model, expected to be called Nemotron 4. Earlier versions of U.S. AI models have lagged well behind China’s free models, which were downloaded roughly 2 billion times this year, far ahead of any Western rival, according to an August report by Hugging Face, the platform where developers share and download AI models. To change that, Nvidia has also agreed to pay almost $13 billion to buy Hugging Face . Governments building their own models mostly start from a free one made by Meta or Alibaba, and Nvidia’s spending is meant to make Nemotron the base they pick instead, Einstein said. The Poolside deal “appears less about displacing incumbent model families and more about increasing future adoption of Nemotron within an ecosystem where Nvidia already has a strong hardware position,” Einstein said. 双 11 这个原本属于国内消费者的购物节，也在被淘宝改造成内销商家低成本试水海外市场的入口。 淘宝加码中大件出口 ]article_adlist--> 9 月 21 日，淘宝公布今年双 11 海外玩法。平台将通过流量、物流和经营能力升级，帮助商家用同一间店、同一批商品同时经营国内与海外市场，实现“一份投入、两盘生意，国内照常卖、海外新增量”。 淘宝出海业务负责人叶天 淘宝出海业务负责人叶天介绍，今年淘宝双 11 将在全球 20 个市场同步启动， 13 个国家和地区提供包邮服务。其中，中国香港、中国澳门、新加坡和马来西亚实现“ 0 门槛包邮”。出海商品从轻小件进一步拓展至家具、家装建材等中件、大件品类， 90% 以上中大件商品将实现海外直邮。 今年双 11 将有超过 120 万淘宝天猫商家参与出海。流量层面，淘宝将“推好店”作为今年双 11 的重要策略，从品质、特色、价格力和服务四个维度识别好店，放大服饰、美妆、家居、宠物等品类的特色供给优势，并在首页增加海外流量入口，上线 Discover 频道、海外榜单和清单等。 公开数据显示，今年上半年跨境电商出口海外仓增长 3.3 倍，全国已有 1.4 亿人通过跨境电商全球购物，有进出口业务的企业增加 11.5 万家，仅用半年超过了去年的规模。与此同时，小包直发模式承压，海外仓备货加速，行业从“轻小件铺货”向“中件大件 + 前置备货”迁移。 物流层面，淘宝将进一步拓展中大件商品的跨境运输能力。目前，中国香港、中国澳门、中国台湾、新加坡、马来西亚、韩国、柬埔寨、澳大利亚、加拿大、菲律宾等 10 个国家和地区均可实现中大件商品跨境直邮，丢包、破损等情况由平台兜底。 “以往部分商家入库拒收的主要原因是物品体积过大，或者重量超重，导致仓库判断无法按照正常流程进行国际段运输，拒收后商家会受到订单和国内物流费用的双重损失。”叶天说，针对家具和家装行业，淘宝推出“ 0 拒收”专项保障，符合条件的商品发出后即可入仓。 ]article_adlist--> 为什么是现在？ 淘宝出海并非今年才启动。 公开资料显示，淘宝的出海业务始于 2016 年。在此之前数年，上淘宝“反向海淘”已成为一些海外华人圈的流行趋势，但受制于物流、支付等基础设施，费时费力，售后也存在极大不确定性。 2016 年至 2021 年，淘宝着手建设跨境出海基础设施。 2025 年，淘宝建成覆盖 20 个国家的直邮体系，部分国家实现跨境包邮。 2026 年，淘宝将战略重点转向“好店时代”。 然而，当前国际贸易环境、关税政策和消费预期的不确定性仍在加剧，中国跨境电商赛道也已挤满专业玩家。此时加码出海仍是好时机吗？ 叶天认为，全球跨境海淘已十分普遍且方便，但淘宝供给的丰富、多样、高品质依然具备不可替代性。 淘宝平台数据显示，其出海业务 GMV 已连续六年实现双位数增长，超过 15 万商家出海后实现年同比翻倍增长。 2025 年双 11 对比 2024 年同期，境外消费者选购商品件单价出现不同程度的增长，其中日本增长 50% 、澳洲增长 15% 、中国香港增长 10% 。高价值用户（单笔消费支出 500 元以上）增速达 10% ，占比同比上升。在淘宝特色核心品类上，消费升级的趋势也十分明显，女装、户外行业，件单价增长 10% ；美妆、箱包等行业增长达到 15% ；彩妆增长 20% 、宠物行业的增长更达到 50% 之多。 过去一轮由中国供应链、极致性价比和平台流量推动的跨境电商增长，正在进入新阶段：海外消费者的需求从“有没有中国商品”走向“能不能买到中国好商品”；中国商家从追求单次卖货，转向经营品牌认知和消费者复购；关税、物流、合规和本地化成本上升，商家需要更低风险的出海方式；跨境平台的竞争，也从“抢商品、抢低价”转向“抢好货、抢优质供给”。 “外部环境越不确定，商家越需要降低试错成本。”叶天认为，国际贸易环境、关税政策和消费预期的不确定性加剧，反而让“低门槛、低风险”的出海方式变得稀缺。淘宝出海要做的，是把出海从“重投入”变成“一项可持续经营的能力”，商家不需要另开店、不需要单独备货、不需要自建海外团队，就能以最低成本试水海外市场。 对做跨境 B2C 的中大型卖家而言，海外仓几乎是履约能力的代名词。谁拥有海外仓，谁就掌握了时效和成本优势。但对于小微型卖家来说，当平台把仓储、物流、清关、售后等跨境履约能力内化为可共享的基础设施，“谁不用建海外仓”则为他们增加了新的竞争力来源。 跨境电商的竞争逻辑正在发生转移：从争夺少数具备外贸能力的专业卖家，转向激活平台上数以百万计的国内商家。淘宝的底牌是内贸商家池的宽度——超过 120 万商家参与出海，覆盖从螺丝钉到地板革的广泛品类。 ]article_adlist--> 中国制造“轻出海” 2025 年，一名马来西亚客户循着货源找到了医尔顿，想要购买几万平方米地板革，总价几十万元。对这家中小企业而言，这笔单子不算小。然而，团队前前后后聊了几轮，跨境物流怎么走、时效能不能保证、售后出了问题谁兜底，每一环节的未知，让他们最终没敢接单。 医尔顿建材旗舰店运营总监贾汉青表示，“有询单却无法落地”几乎是他们启动出海业务之前的常态。传统出海方式的账不难算，组建 10 至 20 人的运营团队，自建海外仓租仓备货，资金投入大几百万起步。这个门槛让他们即使背靠义乌供应链、在建材施工行业扎根 15 年，也只能任由海外买家流失。 转折来自平台的发力。 2026 年初，医尔顿接入淘宝出海增长计划：只需完成上架和售前，把货送到国内集运仓，后续的国际物流、清关、售后、本地退货均交给平台。这意味着，按照传统方式需要大几百万投入的工作，接入平台后“一键就能起跑”。靠着现有运营团队，不到半年，其海外营收增幅接近 200% 。 商家分享 主营国内紧固密封件业务的深圳固万基，线上渠道约占整体销售额的 55% ，淘宝为最重要的线上销售渠道。该公司总经理叶军表示， 2023 年，一笔来自越南的急单让它看到了新的市场空间。一位客户将工厂迁往越南后，急需高强度合金钢螺栓，但当地缺少配套供应，只能从固安机下单一千多元，先发往广西再转运越南。 这笔订单金额不大，指向的问题却不小：制造环节向东南亚延伸，工业供应链的配套并没有同步跟上。紧固件密度高、货值相对低，自行跨境运输时物流成本可占总成本的 10% 以上，“有时候单件货物的运输成本就超过了货值本身”。加入淘宝出海后，他们只需要把货送到集运仓，后续工作和成本均不用承担，直接让其海外月成交额超过 60 万元，今年 1 至 9 月海外成交额同比增长超过 30% ，新加坡、菲律宾等市场表现突出。 对贾汉青他们来说，即便计入跨境运费，不少地区的跨境综合成本仍低于当地采购，供应链价差为跨境物流留出了实在的利润空间。从履约效率看，过去企业自行对接中转仓，海外订单从发货到客户验收大约需要 20 多天，慢的时候可能要等一个多月；接入平台流程后，货到集运仓再到客户签收，只需要一周左右，周期缩短了一半还多。此前一批发往海外的塑胶地板在跨境运输中破损，平台还按赔付标准承担了损失。 大量像医尔顿和固万基这样的中小微中国制造商，正在像“毛细血管”一样加速接入全球贸易。这种延伸的根基是中国工业供应链的深度和韧性。比如，紧固件行业一家工厂最多生产几千种，客户需要的却是“一站式配齐”，这让跨境刚需凸显：越南工厂买不到的螺栓，深圳的仓库里全都能快速配齐。为此，叶军也把一些国内并不常用的配件做成标品提前存在了仓库。 贾汉青说，东南亚客户偏爱深色大花型地板革，这类花色在国内几乎无人问津，“团队索性专门开模、调试、定制交付”。出海不只是把国内商品卖出去，而是以国内供应链的柔性能力，去匹配海外市场的差异化需求。 更大的背景是，中国的家具、家装建材等品类在全球具有明显的国际竞争力。海关数据显示， 2026 年前 8 个月家具及其零件出口额同比微增 0.6% ，这一增长是在欧美抬高贸易壁垒的背景下实现的。在传统外贸渠道收窄的趋势下，跨境电商成为一条能够绕开部分壁垒的替代路径。 对于益好旗舰店这样的定制照片冲印商家，出海逻辑有所不同。其创始人郭志强自 2013 年起自研智能设计与柔性生产系统，让零散订单也能自动设计、报价、拆单。这套能力先在淘宝国内渠道验证， 2019 年试水跨境后成为首批签约商家。 2026 年截至 9 月，海外成交 GMV 同比增长超过 20% ，海外业务占整体收入接近 10% 。 确定性仍是当下全球生意中最为稀缺的因素。对于参与其中的商家，真正的考验可能在双 11 之后。医尔顿的规划是：短期继续用国内库存试水，把东南亚一个个国家、规格跑透；中期等订单密度起来，再把施工班底和本地服务落下去。 更大的挑战来自中国供应链与平台之间的竞争。当“轻出海”成为共识，差异化将来自于供应链的深度、履约的稳定性和对细分品类的理解能力。淘宝的底牌是内贸商家池的宽度。但宽度能否转化为深度，取决于平台能否在不同品类中分别解决“最后一公里”的问题：工业品需要的是快速配货和标准对接，建材需要的是施工落地，定制印刷品需要的是柔性产能与本地合规的适配。   应美利坚合众国总统特朗普邀请，国家主席习近平将于9月23日至25日对美国进行国事访问。   这是习近平主席时隔3年再次到访美国，也将是中美元首半年内实现互访，具有历史性、里程碑意义。   大洋两岸、全球各地，人们共同期待，面对百年变局加速演进、国际形势变乱交织，中美关系这艘巨轮能在两国元首领航掌舵下，穿越风浪，驶入一个新的航程，为动荡不安的世界带去信心和力量。    把舵定向，引领大国正确相处之道   中美两国能不能跨越“修昔底德陷阱”，开创大国关系新范式？能不能携手应对全球性挑战，为世界注入更多稳定性？能不能着眼两国人民福祉和人类前途命运，共同开创两国关系美好未来？   今年5月，北京人民大会堂，习近平主席同来华进行国事访问的特朗普总统会谈，以“历史之问、世界之问、人民之问”道出中美两个大国肩负的时代责任。   中美关系是当今世界最重要的双边关系。50多年前，中美两国领导人以非凡的勇气和智慧，实现“跨越太平洋的握手”。50多年来，中美关系虽历经波折起伏，却总能找到不断向前的力量。   元首外交是中美关系的“指南针”和“定盘星”。   新时代以来，从安纳伯格庄园初次深谈，到华盛顿“白宫秋叙”，从海湖庄园奠定建设性基调，到斐洛里庄园开辟新愿景，习近平主席历次访美，都为中美关系发展把舵领航，引领两国关系平稳前行。   特朗普总统2025年开启第二任期以来，两国元首保持密切联系——去年10月在韩国釜山面对面会晤，今年5月在北京历史性会晤，多次通电话和书信往来，促进相互理解，加深彼此信任，推进务实合作，校准双边关系航向，为动荡世界注入宝贵的确定性、稳定性。   “我愿同特朗普总统共同为中美关系这艘大船领好航、掌好舵，让2026年成为中美关系继往开来的历史性、标志性年份。”习近平主席说。   “两国元首历次会晤最重要的成果是建立信任。”美中贸易全国委员会会长谭森说，美国商界对此最为关注，因为“一旦信任建立，其他事情都会更加容易”。   在北京，习近平主席同特朗普总统就构建“中美建设性战略稳定关系”达成重要共识，为未来3年乃至更长时间的中美关系提供战略指引。   “‘中美建设性战略稳定关系’不是一句口号，而应该是相向而行的行动。”习近平主席从四个维度阐释这一新定位的核心要义：合作为主的积极稳定，竞争有度的良性稳定，分歧可控的常态稳定，和平可期的持久稳定。   8月25日，第三届中美1.5轨对话在北京举行，双方政界、战略界和商界代表围绕“建设性战略稳定——新时代中美务实合作”深入交流，一致认为应共同落实好两国元首达成的重要共识，加强沟通对话，增进政治互信，开展各领域合作。   太平洋足够大，容得下中美两国共同发展、各自繁荣。实现中华民族伟大复兴和让美国再次伟大，完全可以并行不悖、相互成就、造福世界。   “纵观中美关系发展历程，能不能做到相互尊重、和平共处、合作共赢是双边关系能否稳定发展的关键所在。”习近平主席始终强调，中美应该做伙伴、做朋友，携手多办一些有利于两国和世界的大事、实事、好事。   从推动解决国际和地区热点问题，到应对全球性挑战，再到支持多边机制发展，中美携手合作发挥建设性作用，是两国人民所愿，也是世界人民所盼。   中美两个大国携手合作“对世界所有国家而言都意义非凡”，全球智库席勒研究所联合国官方代表理查德·布莱克说。      互利共赢，不断拉长合作清单   秋日的厦门，第二十六届中国国际投资贸易洽谈会上，中美省州投资贸易合作交流活动备受关注。双方从地方到企业，保持良好合作势头。   “美企没有撤离中国，对华投资正从规模布局转向深耕增值。”华南美国商会会长哈利·赛亚丁说，据这家商会的调查结果，75%的受访美企2026年拟对华再投资。   中美经贸关系的本质是互利共赢。习近平主席5月会见随特朗普总统访华的美国知名企业高管时指出，美国企业正在深度参与中国改革开放，双方都从中获益，“中方欢迎美国对华加强互利合作”。      2026年7月31日，在美国华盛顿，中国贸促会组织中国企业家代表团与美中贸易全国委员会及其会员企业交流座谈。新华社记者 李睿 摄   “美中是世界上两个最大、最具活力、技术最先进的经济体，两国经济关系至关重要、不可或缺。”美中贸易全国委员会会长谭森说。   从投资到贸易，从传统产业到创新领域，中美有着广泛的共同利益和广阔的合作空间。加强对话与协商，拉长合作清单，压缩问题清单，是两国的普遍期待。   数据显示，尽管面临摩擦和挑战，中美贸易展现出强大韧性，今年第二季度双边货物贸易额同比增长13.7%。截至今年7月，美国在华累计设立外资企业已超8.4万家。   按照两国元首的共识，中美经贸团队举行多轮磋商，稳定两国经贸关系和市场预期，为维护全球产业链供应链稳定发挥重要作用。   “中美‘合则两利、斗则俱伤’是经过实践反复验证的常识，中美‘相互成就、共同繁荣’是看得见、摸得着的实景。”习近平主席指明了中美关系的正确方向。   今年是“十五五”开局之年，中国正在以高质量发展全面推进中国式现代化。今年也是美国独立250周年。两国进入各自发展关键阶段，新的合作机遇不断涌现。   不久前，中国企业家代表团访问美国盐湖城、芝加哥、华盛顿等地，同120余家美国企业和机构座谈。双方合作意愿依然强劲，共享“中国机遇2.0”的共识加速凝聚。       2026年4月30日，观众在第九届数字中国建设峰会现场体验区的特斯拉展位参观。新华社记者 林善传 摄   中国超大的市场规模、完善的产业体系和蓬勃的创新活力，为包括美国企业在内的全球企业提供广阔舞台。美国行业人士普遍认为，在绿色能源、数字经济、人工智能、生物医药等前沿领域，两国企业合作潜力巨大。   代表约70家企业的俄亥俄州哥伦布中美商会会长凯特·沙利文说，从两国合资太阳能电池板企业“照亮美国”公司的成功运营中，可以看到美中合作的机遇和潜能，“两国企业合作建立在广泛的、真实的供需关系之上”。   “期待两国元首保持战略沟通，带给市场和两国企业更稳定、长期的预期和信心。”美中绿色能源促进会会长王麒说。    相知相亲，夯实两国关系民意基础   今年8月，北京首都体育学院内，一场别开生面的中美匹克球友谊赛气氛热烈。来自美国艾奥瓦州的师生同中国青少年混合组队、切磋球艺，初次见面的年轻人迅速成为伙伴。   无论形势如何变化，中美两国人民交流合作的愿望不会改变。55年前，中美“乒乓外交”成就“小球转动大球”的历史佳话。如今，起源于美国的匹克球“成为中美两国青少年交流的新纽带”。   “中美关系希望在人民，基础在民间，未来在青年，活力在地方。”   2015年在西雅图，习近平主席发表演讲，“中美两国虽然相距遥远，但两国人民友好交往源远流长”的话语拉近心灵的距离；   2017年在海湖庄园，习近平主席同特朗普总统会晤，提出“人文交流是两国关系的地基”，强调应夯实两国关系民意基础，给中美关系长期健康发展提供更多正能量；   2023年在旧金山，习近平主席讲述一个个中美友谊的故事，一句“人民友谊之树已经长大，一定能经风历雨”引发全场共鸣。      2023年8月8日，在中国重庆史迪威博物馆举行的约瑟夫·史迪威将军诞辰140周年纪念活动上，嘉宾参观史迪威将军生平图片展。新华社记者 王全超 摄   多年来，从访问美国塔科马市林肯中学到连续多年给艾奥瓦州老朋友送上新春祝福，从会见史迪威将军后人、飞虎队老兵，到复信美国肯恩大学校长寄语两国教育交流与合作，习近平主席同美国各界民众温暖互动，鼓励他们“为推动中美关系稳定、健康、可持续发展作出新贡献”。   2023年旧金山之行，习近平主席郑重宣布中方“未来5年愿邀请5万名美国青少年来华交流学习”，期待“两国人民多走动、多来往、多交流，共同续写新时代两国人民友好的故事”。    2026年7月17日，在南京市第一中学，中美青少年在音乐展演彩排间隙交流。新华社记者 李博 摄   这份邀约得到中美青少年热情回应。短短两年多，已有来自全美50个州的超过5万名美国青少年来到中国，深入沿海和内陆，走进雪域高原、江南水乡，探访智能工厂、美丽乡村，感知中国、结下友谊。    2024年5月16日，在美国首都华盛顿，艾奥瓦州友人卢卡·贝隆（右二）等在《我的中国相册》颁奖仪式上分享与中国的故事。新华社记者 刘杰 摄   “我特别感谢习近平主席提出这一倡议，其影响非常深远。”同习近平主席有着40多年友谊的艾奥瓦州友人卢卡·贝隆说，人文交流，特别是青少年之间的交流，对巩固中美关系非常重要。      2026年7月7日，《黑神话：悟空》游戏和音乐爱好者在美国洛杉矶孔雀剧院门前拍照。新华社发（曾慧摄） items.title: 台行政院长吁抵御小红书、抖音等“文化入侵”
items.desc: 赖清德说，他三年前竞选总统时提出“文化永续、世界台湾”的政策蓝图，承诺持续增加文化预算，并推动跨部门及中央与地方合作的文化治理。对于文化部预算近两年遭立法院大幅删减或冻结，他感到“非常错愕”，但强调政府不会停止推动文化发展。
items.articleText: 台行政院长吁抵御小红书、抖音等“文化入侵” 台湾行政院长卓荣泰呼吁文化界团结起来，对内抵制删减、冻结文化预算的“文化杀手”，对外抵御小红书、抖音等平台带来的“文化入侵”。 综合台湾《联合报》《中国时报》报道，卓荣泰星期天（9月20日）出席文化会议并致辞约10分钟。他在演讲的前七分钟细数百大文化基地、文化币、大阪世博和“黑潮计划”等文化政策与成果，并表示希望政府在文化领域扮演的角色从“补助”转向“支持”。 卓荣泰随后将话题转向文化部预算遭大幅删减和冻结。他说，文化部的宣传费用、公共电视和影视局的经费，以及文策院的人才培训费用均遭删减，“这些都是对文化界极大极大的伤害”。 他强调：“文化界应该要团结起来，有能力对内抗拒这种文化的杀手。” 谈及“外来文化入侵”时，卓荣泰点名影视作品、语言文字，以及小红书和抖音等社交媒体，称这些文化正不断进入台湾，尤其影响青少年。 延伸阅读 台陆委会：小红书封禁八月 诈骗案数量锐减逾七成 人民日报：上半年台湾民众赴陆人次同比增24.9% 他说，如果没有办法保护台湾本土文化的主体性，外来文化的入侵会侵蚀到民主宪政的基本精神、也会侵蚀到本土文化好不容易建立起来起步、而且非常快速起飞的基础。 卓荣泰表示，文化会议的总结将提交行政院文化会报讨论。政府也将持续检讨如何应对内部的“文化杀手”和外来的“文化入侵”，“用政府的力量协助本土文化产业发展，用国家的力量保护本土的文化产业”。 除卓荣泰外，台湾总统赖清德和文化部长李远致辞时，也谈到文化预算遭删减的问题。 李远说，在赖清德和卓荣泰支持下，文化预算逐年增加，并以达到中央政府总预算的1％为目标。但文化部预算增加并成为重要议题后，近两年也面对不少政治攻防。今年文化预算仍遭大幅删减，公共媒体和文化创意产业等领域受到影响，宣传费用更连续两年遭删。 赖清德说，他三年前竞选总统时提出“文化永续、世界台湾”的政策蓝图，承诺持续增加文化预算，并推动跨部门及中央与地方合作的文化治理。对于文化部预算近两年遭立法院大幅删减或冻结，他感到“非常错愕”，但强调政府不会停止推动文化发展。 卓荣泰 赖清德 文化 台湾 小红书 抖音 两岸关系 上一篇 中美元首峰会前夕 李成钢任中国国际贸易谈判代表 下一篇 月之暗面推出金融解决方案 数十家机构采用 购买此文章

items.title: 埃利奥特·马奇（ Elliot March ）让景观引领潮流
items.desc: MAWD联合创始人着眼于景观、建筑和房源的特色，塑造有归属感的空间
items.articleText: When Elliot March was a student at the University of Edinburgh, a chance meeting led to a successful partnership. “James White and I were late to the same class,” he says. “We immediately connected over a shared curiosity about architecture and design.” Early in their careers, both men worked at larger practices, continuing to learn and refine their craft. White became increasingly drawn to interiors and exploring how they shape an individual’s experience. Eventually, the pair branched out and established MAWD | March and White Design in 2010. The two friends treasured this newfound freedom to think more holistically about projects and develop their own point of view. March has led MAWD’s evolution from a luxury British interior design firm to the globally recognized practice it is today. The team has completed a range of projects across sectors, from hospitality to residential to yachts. No matter the size or scale of a room, March is less interested in arriving with a particular look in mind. “I’d rather let the architecture, location, light, materials, and daily life of a space lead us somewhere,” he says. “When all of those things come together naturally, the result feels like it belongs there.” Today, Elliot March joins us for Friday Five ! Here, he shares five locations that inspire him and five projects that reflect his work. Elliot March’s Inspirations Photography courtesy of Elliot March 1. Wynwood Walls I’ve been spending a lot more time in Miami’s Wynwood neighborhood through my work on The Cloud One Hotel & Residences Wynwood , and it always gives me something new to look at. I love the energy of the murals against the area’s industrial backdrop and the constant tension between raw materials and expression. That contrast has stayed with me as we’ve thought about how the project can feel connected to Wynwood rather than simply placed within it. Photography courtesy of Elliot March 2. Paso Robles Wineries I’m drawn to the wineries around Paso Robles, California, for their relationship with the landscape and how architecture can feel quiet within it. The local stone, timber, concrete, and weathered materials have a particular quality that feels both grounded and tactile. I also love the way the buildings frame the surrounding vineyards rather than competing with them. It’s a landscape where material, light, and nature do much of the work. Photography courtesy of Elliot March 3. Yucca Valley Cycling through Yucca Valley, California, around sunset is one of my favorite ways to clear my head. The landscape changes so quickly at that hour. The colors get warmer, the shadows stretch out, and suddenly things you’ve passed a hundred times look completely different. I love that reminder to slow down and really look. Some of the best ideas come from noticing what is already there. Photography courtesy of Elliot March 4. Parte Vieja I love wandering through the Parte Vieja quarter in San Sebastián, Spain, because the details have so much character. The worn stone, painted façades, balconies, timber, tiled thresholds, and layers of history all sit together without feeling overly considered. It’s the kind of environment where you can spend an afternoon simply looking up and noticing things. I’m always interested in places that have developed organically over time, where the imperfections and traces of use are part of what makes them beautiful. Photography courtesy of Elliot March 5. Taos Pueblo I find the Taos Pueblo historic site in New Mexico incredibly moving. There’s a directness to the architecture found in the local materials and simple forms, and an unmistakable relationship to the landscape gives it so much warmth and presence. Nothing feels arbitrary. It’s a place that reminds me how meaningful architecture can be when it grows out of its environment, its materials, and the people who have shaped it over time. 5 MAWD Projects Photography by VMI Studio 1. The Cloud One Hotel & Residences Wynwood The Cloud One Hotel & Residences Wynwood is meaningful to me because of how much inspiration we have been able to draw from Wynwood itself. I’ve always been interested in neighborhoods where different histories and influences sit side by side, and Wynwood has that in abundance, from its warehouse and garment-district past to the art and creative energy that define it today. We wanted to capture some of that character through exposed concrete, wild oak, bronze, lush planting, and art curated by Goldman Global Arts , while still creating a place that feels calm and comfortable. I love that balance between the energy outside and the sense of retreat within. Photography by Evan Joseph 2. The Greenwich by Rafael Viñoly The Greenwich in Manhattan’s Financial District is especially personal to me. The late architect Rafael Viñoly invited MAWD to lead the interiors, prompting my move from London to New York and, shortly after, the opening of our New York headquarters. It also gave us the chance to bring our superyacht design experience into a Manhattan residential setting. The bookmatched Noir Saint Laurent marble behind the front desk, with its subtle nautical quality, is one example. I love that the project represents both a new creative chapter for MAWD and a pivotal one for me personally. Photography courtesy of Strategic Property Partners 3. Water Street Tampa What draws me to the forthcoming residences at Water Street Tampa is the relationship between the architecture and the way people live there. Tampa has this wonderful indoor-outdoor rhythm, so we started by looking at the building’s portals, louvers, and courtyards and thinking about how some of that language could carry through to the interiors. The light and tropical landscape gave us permission to be a little more expressive with color and material. I love projects where the location pushes you somewhere you might not have gone otherwise, and this has been one of those. Photography courtesy of Related Ross 4. Edgeworth What excites me

items.title: AI或毁灭人类之争白热化：行业领袖促全行业放缓 监管与动机受质疑

items.desc: 在多起 #AI 突破隔离并实施攻击的事件引发警报后，Anthropic首席执行官达阿莫代伊与OpenAI首席执行官阿尔特曼呼吁全球行业放缓研发步伐，以降低存在性风险。批评者质疑这一呼吁背后的商业动机及第三方评估机构的独立性， #白宫 AI顾问大卫·萨克斯指责相关机构与企业利益纠缠。政治层面分歧明显：总统 #川普 及多名共和党人反对新增监管护栏，而部分议员主张

2026-09-16T09:15:43-07:00 AI 毁灭人类 人工智能 川普 白宫 【希望之声2026年9月16日】（本台记者陈雯韵综合编译） 关于 人工智能 （ AI ）对人类构成生存性威胁的近一个世纪的辩论在本月被全面引爆，因为在该技术多次“逃逸出隔离”的事件之后， AI 领域领袖和研究人员敦促全行业放缓步伐。 上周，Anthropic研究员雅各布·考克森辞职，并警告称，他的前雇主以及其竞争对手Open AI （他此前在该公司工作多年）正在与时间赛跑，将可能“在本十年末把我们全部杀死”的技术推向市场。” Anthropic的埃文·胡宾格也表示业内其他人持相同观点，并称他将到2030年人类灭绝的风险评估为超过10%。 尽管批评者对考克森的动机以及顶级 AI 公司与所谓负责调查近期“失控”事件的第三方调查团队之间盘根错节的资金关系提出质疑，但本周末顶级 AI 领袖呼吁全球放缓。 Anthropic首席执行官达里奥·阿莫代伊周六撰文警告，如果行业不能就放慢开发步伐达成一致，那么类似Open AI -Hugging Face攻击中涉及的 AI 蜂群“可能在短短6至12个月内，凭借一个持久性的僵尸网络，接管整个互联网”。阿莫代伊表示，“进展仍将显得很快，我们必须明智地利用争取到的时间。” Open AI 首席执行官萨姆·阿尔特曼周六与阿莫代伊一道呼吁行业放缓，并表示他将承诺给予独立评估人员“类似员工的访问权限。” 与此同时，围绕该技术如果达到人工通用智能（AGI）——即机器在广泛能力上超越人类的门槛——可能以何种方式实质性 毁灭人类 ，以及是否需要、需要何种监管以跟上飞速发展的步伐的辩论不断升温。 在业界得知一群Open AI 智能体利用零日漏洞从测试沙盒逃逸并攻破Hugging Face（一个用于 AI 模型和机器学习的平台）后，关于 AI 突破隔离的讨论达到白热化。 这些 AI 被赋予一个不可能完成的任务，并推理认为作弊是取胜的最佳选项。 在该事件发生前的数周内，另一群Open AI 智能体劫持了DseWiki及其他数个wiki类网站，并在七周内累计进行了超过14,000次编辑。 Civ AI 研究负责人安德鲁·尹对大纪元时报表示，“我们只是不了解[他们的动机]，所以我们可以推测，我认为我们在这里可以做出一个相当合理的推测，即那些滥用这些维基条目相互协调的智能体并不需要作弊”，“看起来他们是在尝试进行快速数据检索” 在Hugging Face事件公布后的数日内，Anthropic表示其三款 AI 模型在测试评估期间曾入侵三家外部机构，Meta也在8月上旬承认发生了类似的 AI 入侵。另一起由发现该维基攻击的团队标注的事件显示，Open AI 智能体向Ruby编程语言的代码库分发网站RubyGems上传了数百个恶意文件包。 对“ AI 失控”叙事的批评者指出，Open AI 和Anthropic在对其内部模型进行评估测试时刻意放松了某些安全协议，导致了隔离失效。也有人认为，这项技术的行为仍在背离执行 AI 训练的人类评估者的意图。这再次点燃并加剧了一个近一个世纪的争论：如果 AI 超越人类的认知能力，它是否注定会 毁灭人类 。 如果是，那么 AI 将如何做到这一点？ 对 AI 的生存性恐惧并不新鲜，自这一概念激发人类想象以来便已存在。 1951年，作为最早研究 AI 的计算机科学家和数学家之一的艾伦·图灵预言，这项技术终有一天会超出人类控制。 在该十年末期，数学家诺伯特·维纳发出警告称，智能机器最终会转而实现自身目标，而人类将无法阻止它们。“机器将会做我们让它们做的事情，而不是我们本该让它们做的事情，”维纳在一篇20世纪50年代的文章中写道。“我们可以谦逊些，在机器的帮助下过上美好生活，或者我们可以自大并走向死亡。” 即便在这项技术达到“递归自我改进”（即无需人类干预即可自我提升的能力）甚至实现AGI之前，专家们也已指出，不法行为者——无论境内还是境外——可能利用 AI 入侵敏感的计算机系统或基础设施。 Anthropic上周发布的一份报告中概述了这一点，报告称其挫败了与伊朗和中国政权相关的账号群体的企图，这些账号群体当时在跟踪美国海军动向并监视记者和宗教团体。 如今，代理型 AI 已被证明能够突破隔离并自主行动，专家警告称该技术可能瞄准关键基础设施，包括公用事业电网、国家的网络安全基础设施以及生物医学实验室。一些研究人员警告称，从理论上讲，任何连接到互联网的系统都可能暴露于自主 AI 蜂群攻击之下，并被武器化用于对抗人类，包括医院、大学、核电站、水电大坝以及某些军事平台。 “不幸的是，我们生活在一个不同的世界，那里正在进行着……‘太空竞赛’，而所有这些公司都试图尽可能快地推进，”尹说。“而激励总是会推动人们朝着更快推进、走捷径的方向前进。 这就是会发生的事情。” 围绕“可能杀死人类的 AI ”的辩论持续存在，其背景是该领域的两大领先竞争者——Open AI 和Anthropic——正陷入一场全行业竞赛，力图将高度先进的产品版本推向市场，并兑现对该技术能力的持续承诺。 两家公司也在努力满足投资者并提升估值，为最终上市做准备，Anthropic希望在年底前实现这一目标。 Open AI 则将IPO首秀目标定在2027年的某个时间，此前其最初计划在今年推出。 领先的科技投资人兼 AI 评论员加文·贝克周日表示，他相信阿莫代伊在没有全球放缓技术的情况下有关 AI 对人类威胁的表述是出于真诚，但他指出，“所有这一切从长期来看也可能有利于他的业务。” 另一些人也对被指派审核近期代理型 AI 入侵事件的第三方评估机构的独立性表示担忧，尤其是分析了Hugging Face事件的“模型评估与威胁研究”（METR）。 “别再假装METR是独立的，当它与Anthropic的投资者和员工纠缠不清时，” 白宫 AI 顾问大卫·萨克斯周六表示。“别再假装你需要同样的评估者去监管那些甚至不处于前沿的竞争对手。” 萨克斯鼓励阿莫代伊和阿尔特曼如果他们所称的内部模型确实像两人所暗示的那样可怕，就按他们的说法去“为前沿设定节奏”，通过放慢自身开发来实现，但他认为，这些公司可以在不要求“偏好的监管框架”的情况下做到这一点，如果他们不自愿这样做，就将构成“监管俘获”或“选举季心理战”。 萨克斯等人认为，潜在的放缓从理论上可能使Open AI 和Anthropic在更广泛的行业中稳居前列，甚至有人指称，考克森和类似的行业研究人员是亲民主党团体在一场充满争议的中期选举周期前协调开展的公关活动的一部分。 总统 川普 在周一（14日）更进一步表示，给 AI 加设额外护栏没有必要，政府已经对这些公司拥有“巨大的刑事和监管权力！”“正在针对 AI 和数据中心进行一场病态的阴谋，唯一对此感到高兴的是中国，” 川普 补充说。“谁赢得 AI ，谁就获胜！许多共和党人呼应了这一观点。 即便如此，近几周来自左翼和右翼的 AI 监管呼声此起彼伏。尽管如此，目前尚不清楚在11月选举前，国会是否会在这方面有所行动。 参议院多数党领袖约翰·图恩（共和党-南达科他州）周一表示，可以在不让中国在该技术上领先于美国的情况下应对假设性的 AI 风险，但这需要“轻度干预。” 众议院议长迈克·约翰逊（共和党-路易斯安那州）周二驳斥了 AI
